pages.title: Mantle Geodynamics
pages.text: $(thing)Mantle Geodynamics$()$(br2)The mantle is solid rock, and yet it flows: a centimetre a year, heated from below, cooled from above, turning over like a pot on a stove. Its minerals - ringwoodite, bridgmanite - only exist under its pressure.

$(thing)Insight$(): 80$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Plate Tectonics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Ringwoodite, 2 Bridgmanite.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A layer of thickness L is heated from below by a temperature difference ΔT. Whether it turns over depends on one number: buoyancy (ρ g α ΔT) against heat diffusion κ and viscosity μ. Write that number, N.
